A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. V1 Appendices A–C correspond to v2 Appendices B–D; v2 adds an explanatory Appendix A.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figure 1 report original Monte Carlo simulations of estimation error across embedding dimensions and activation smoothness levels, with procedures in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains the original simulations and empirical convergence slopes in Section 5 and Figure 1, with procedures in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The bilinear interaction model, empirical-risk estimator, and alternating spline/MLP, Adam, and ridge-regression procedure are retained. New Appendix A explains the existing attention surrogate rather than introducing a different implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic interaction-estimation task with uniformly sampled tokens, Gaussian noise, and spline-generated activations. No datasets, domains, or evaluation scenarios are added.

E2.justification: Both compare empirical convergence with theoretical reference rates, without evaluating competing algorithms. The newly cited attention methods appear only in related work.

E3.justification: Appendix C in v1 and Appendix D in v2 retain identical experimental settings, including N=3, the five training sizes from 20,000 to 70,000, 2,000 test samples, and interaction-function test MSE. The added theoretical assumption does not change the simulated data.

E4.justification: Figure 1 retains the same analyses of convergence across embedding dimensions and spline degrees. No ablations, robustness tests, error analyses, or additional empirical case studies are introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 300 seeds in Table 1 and median-across-seed markers in Figure 1. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests, or a different uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 1 is visually identical, including dimension-specific slopes of -0.802, -0.812, and -0.765 and the degree-8 slope of -0.899. The empirical findings and simulation parameter values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Assumption 2.1 adds conditional independence given a sigma-algebra containing the selected token's information; the previous density condition is merely renumbered A3. New Corollary B.2 states an error bound without the rd restriction, explicitly adding an rd(log M)^2/M term. These materially change the formal assumptions and stated guarantees, although most proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: V2 removes 'Dimension-Free' from the title and explicitly conditions the abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion on rd <= (M/log M)^(1/(2β+1)). This narrows the central advertised claim to a regime where the nonparametric term dominates; that condition already appeared in v1's Theorem 3.1.

C2.justification: Remark 3.3 now explains dimension dependence through matrix-estimation error and removes the suggestion that rougher activations tolerate larger dimensions. New Appendix A clarifies the constant-value and frozen-normalization simplifications connecting the existing surrogate to softmax attention, and discusses particle-specific nonlinearities as a possible extension.

D1.justification: The simulation appendix retains the same data-generation instructions, initialization, architecture, optimizers, regularization, training budgets, and parameter table. Its move from Appendix C to D adds no implementation or resource-access information.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds a distinct discussion of nonparametric and semiparametric neural-network estimation, including Horowitz–Mammen, Schmidt-Hieber, and Bhattacharya et al., and expands alternatives to softmax. Appendix A additionally positions the surrogate relative to Geshkovski, Sander, and Bruno. This substantively broadens the research context beyond isolated citation additions.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted revisions to the title, abstract, contribution statement, Remark 3.3, and conclusion; adds explanatory material and a related-work subsection; and performs scattered copyediting. The main section sequence and most existing prose and proofs are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 now interrupts the numerical-simulation narrative instead of following it, and surrounding sections and appendices reflow. The plot graphics, axes, legends, and Table 1 display remain identical; no figures or tables are added.

improvement.justification: V2 improves claim calibration by bringing v1's existing dimensional restriction into the headline claims and clarifying the attention surrogate. However, the new conditional-independence assumption is not incorporated into Lemma 3.4 or its unchanged proof. Moreover, Corollary B.2 claims an rd(log M)^2/M term, whereas its cited bound B.19, using the stated L3,M proportional to (log M)^4, carries a fifth logarithmic power. Clearer exposition therefore coexists with an inadequately justified new guarantee, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
